newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Land dealer denies he was kidnapped by PLO forces.
newsitem.headline: Land dealer denies he was kidnapped by PLO forces.

text.p: An Arab land dealer whom Israel said had been rescued from Palestinian kidnappers denied on Monday he had been abducted, and his son accused the Jewish state of exploiting the incident for political gain.

Israeli police had said they saved Asaad Rajabi on Saturday from Palestinians who allegedly kidnapped him on suspicion of selling Arab land to Jews. The police arrested six Palestinians, among them four members of a PLO security force, for the alleged abduction.

Rajabi, an East Jerusalem resident, told a news conference in Jerusalem on Monday he was voluntarily accompanying Palestinian security agents to the PLO-ruled town of Ramallah when an Israeli force stopped them.
"While we were on the way, the Israeli Defence Forces and the Israeli police abducted us and took us all into Mascobiyeh (police station) and interrogated us," Rajabi said.

Three alleged West Bank land dealers have been killed in the month since the Palestinian Authority announced a ban on the land sales, which a Palestinian cabinet member has called a crime punishable by death.

Israel has blamed the killings on the Palestinian Authority, warning that the incidents threatened the fragile peace process. Israeli police have said they have "solid evidence" linking a Palestinian security force to the killings.

The Palestinian Authority has said it was investigating several suspected land dealers and intended to put them on trial if there were sufficient evidence against them, but denies it was behind the three mens' deaths.

Rajabi's son Usama said the Palestinian security men behaved politely when they knocked at the family door and asked for the father to accompany them. He said his father initially did not want to go but later agreed to accompany them.
Usama said the publicity given to the case was created by Israel to serve its political objectives:
"Israel is interested in enlarging the incident and reaping political gains at our expense. We are not willing to give (them) this opportunity to smear us."
An Israeli police spokeswoman said Rajabi was known to have co-operated with 34-year-old Ali Mohammad Jumhour, the latest land dealer to be killed in the West Bank.
Jamhour was buried on Monday in a quiet funeral attended by about 150 people, witnesses said.
Rajabi confirmed he was a land dealer, but denied he had sold any property to Israelis.

Asked about reports he had sold an East Jerusalem house to Israelis, he said: "Never. I have never sold any property to Jews and neither brokered any deal to Jews. I am new into this business and such dealings are far from me," he said.
